screening_decisions.reason: Double-blind randomized trial of aminophylline vs placebo in patients with acute ischemic stroke; treatment administered as bolus plus 3-day infusion. Timing from onset not explicitly stated, but acute enrollment suggests initiation within one week. Include for full-text confirmation.

Double-blind randomized trial of intravenous aminophylline vs placebo in acute cerebral infarction; immediate post-injection effects assessed. Timing from onset not stated, but acute setting suggests initiation within one week. Include for full-text confirmation.
Not a randomized controlled trial: open-label, single-arm dose-escalation of caffeine+ethanol (caffeinol) despite initiation within 6 hours. Fails the randomized comparator requirement.
Physiological study of vincamin and aminophyllin on cerebral metabolism in unspecified subjects; no confirmed/presumed acute ischemic stroke population and no clear randomized placebo/control design.

Randomized double-blind cross-over study of caffeine vs placebo in patients recovering from acute ischemic stroke; physiological endpoints (CBF/velocity) and timing likely beyond one week post-onset; does not meet 'treatment started within one week' criterion.

Randomized double-blind cross-over caffeine vs placebo with physiological outcomes in patients recovering from stroke; recovery phase suggests treatment not initiated within one week of onset. Fails timing criterion.
Method study of intracarotid aminophylline infusion effects on cerebral blood flow; no randomized placebo/control comparison and not clearly in acute ischemic stroke patients.
Animal study (cats) of aminophylline and other agents on ischemic/non-ischemic cortex; not a randomized clinical trial in humans with acute ischemic stroke.
Animal study (dogs) comparing cardiovascular effects of cetiedil, papaverine, and aminophylline; not a human randomized trial in acute ischemic stroke.
Historical/observational report on aminophylline in cerebral vascular disorders; lacks randomized placebo/control design in acute ischemic stroke with treatment within one week.
